front.title: Verifiable Firewall and Security-Enforcement Metadata in IPv6

abstract.t: This document defines a way to carry a verifiable record of security enforcement inside IPv6 packets. Each firewall (or other security enforcement point) that handles a packet writes a small, authenticated note saying which rule it matched and what action it took. The notes are protected by a chained Integrity Check Value (ICV), reusing the construction defined for In-situ OAM (IOAM) data integrity. A checker can then prove two separate things: that the notes are authentic (not forged or changed on the way), and that the recorded actions match the intended policy. Because the two checks are independent, a firewall that honestly diverges from policy -- for example because of a stale rule or an implementation bug -- still produces an authentic note, and the divergence is reported rather than hidden. Operators thus gain precise per-hop evidence that every enforcement point was traversed and applied the intended policy, so an EP that was skipped or did not enforce is revealed.
